snippets.text: Pelvic inflammatory disease is the result of an infection of internal genitalia, most commonly by Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and mainly affects sexually active females, usually between the ages of 15 and 25 years. A tubo-ovarian abscess (TOA) and pyosalpinx are adnexal manifestations of the disease. A tubo-ovarian abscess most commonly appears as a complex, thick-walled, fluid-filled lesion with internal septa. Pyosalpinx manifests as a fluid-filled tubular adnexal structure with thickened walls.
